headline: Six days out from the crossing, the taper has landed clean. Legs are banked, engine intact, movement holding through the logistics window. The next chapter is written on the trail, not here.
confidence_reasons: Limited data sources active in last 3 days

sections.overview: The picture is exactly what a final taper week should look like: running has thinned to short, easy efforts sitting low in the aerobic range, while the demonstrated fitness underneath — banked from the big long runs and the sharp threshold session late last month — is untouched. Strength held right up to the end of the loading window before quietly stepping back, which is the correct sequencing this close to a sustained demand. What's genuinely reassuring is that steps remain high despite the packing-and-travel phase; the residual movement hasn't collapsed, which matters more than any single run right now. Cardio load reads as "detraining," but that label is meaningless in context — it's measuring the deliberate absence of recent strain, not a loss of capacity. Recovery nights remain the one variable that's still bouncing around, worth noting heading into a demand that will punish accumulated sleep debt.
sections.trends: The medium-term shape is a genuine build that peaked and then intentionally tapered — the recent four-week block ran meaningfully higher than the prior one before the deliberate wind-down. Year-to-date, the contrast with last year is stark: the athlete is carrying multiples of the volume they had at this point in 2025. That's not an accident of a single block; it's a season of accumulated base now being protected rather than extended. The shape makes complete sense for someone maintaining year-round hybrid readiness who has a specific sustained effort imminent — build, bank, then guard.
sections.threshold: Threshold pace has held flat over the last month, and given the taper that stability is the honest read — no reason to expect movement when recent load is deliberately suppressed. The single sharp session on the 25th, sitting well into the upper zones with a genuine chunk of Z4 time, confirms the top-end engine is still accessible and responsive. For the crossing specifically, threshold isn't the currency that matters — durability and time on feet are — but knowing the aerobic ceiling is intact means the easy pace has real margin beneath it.
sections.zones: The recent easy runs sit almost entirely in Z1 with occasional light Z2, which is precisely correct for a taper — the intent is freshness, not stimulus. The one session that broke that pattern, the fast 18 km, was deliberately mixed with substantial Z3/Z4 time and stands out clearly against everything around it as an isolated sharpener rather than a drift into the grey zone. Everything since has been obedient and low. The per-session shapes confirm the distribution is doing its job: the block isn't trying to accomplish adaptation now, it's trying to arrive rested, and the zone profile matches that intent exactly.
sections.hr_comparison: Strength sessions have been logged without HR the last two weeks, so there's no fresh comparison to draw there — the earlier calibrated readings sat sensibly in the low aerobic range, consistent with functional work rather than metabolically brutal sessions. On the running side, HR has tracked pace faithfully across the taper, with the easy efforts producing appropriately suppressed averages and controlled maxes. Nothing in the source agreement looks off.
sections.calendar: The frequency pattern over the final fortnight tells the taper story cleanly: a genuine quiet stretch mid-cycle followed by short, frequent touches to keep the legs turning over without loading them. The strength cadence stepped back a touch as the crossing approached rather than being crammed in, which is the disciplined choice. The consistency underneath all of this — sustained running and strength engagement across the season — is what earns the right to taper without anxiety.
sections.personal_bests: None of the current bests are in play this week and shouldn't be — the taper deliberately suppresses the conditions that produce them, and the imminent focus is a durability event, not a pace one. The short-distance PBs from last autumn remain the relevant benchmarks for when speed work resumes post-crossing; the top-end sharpness shown late last month suggests they're not far out of reach once the calendar allows a proper sharpening block.

watch_items: Watch whether recovery nights steady in the final days before departure — this is the one metric that's stayed variable and the one that compounds most under a multi-day self-supported load.
Once the crossing begins, track how easy-run HR responds to daily pack-loaded efforts stacking up — the first two or three days will redefine what "easy" actually costs.
Note the back-to-back leg response over the opening stretch; early durability under cumulative load is the genuine unknown, not the underlying fitness.
Keep an eye on whether movement holds through the final travel window as a read on residual freshness into the transition.
